card.hook: Picture a red-brick prison with a watchtower by the gate, and a field kitchen parked in the yard like lunch is about to be served. Karosta Prison is that kind of spot, and your phone will love it.
card.stand_here: For a moody warm-up, stand on Zemgales iela, 559 m from the prison with the prison to the west, and face the weathered brick and Soviet-era buildings. For the main shot, walk into the yard of Karostas cietums and face the red-brick building and the watchtower near the entrance.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to take in the whole building, then try 2x for brick texture, peeling surfaces or the tower. If you're standing close and the tower won't fit, drop to 0.5x.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the brick wall, then slide the picture a touch darker so the red keeps its colour and the sky doesn't wash out.
card.best_time: Go in daylight. A bright overcast day is ideal, because the soft light shows off the brick without harsh shadows.
card.selfie_here: Try the courtyard of Karosta Prison (Invalīdu iela 4), next to the old military vehicle on display. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and check the screen to see how much of the building sneaks in behind you, because we couldn't confirm it shows up from this exact spot.
card.rules_and_safety: Some of the old brick buildings around Karosta are boarded up or look unsafe, so don't go inside for a quick look. Photography is generally allowed in public areas, but ask staff about restrictions, and check the official site to confirm the yard is open and whether it's ticketed.
card.challenge: Get the truck, the field kitchen or the amphibious vehicle in the foreground, with the tower peeking out behind it. Bonus points if you look like you're guarding it.
card.good_to_know: Karosta Prison is the red-brick prison building in Karosta, a district of Liepāja. The yard has a military truck, a field kitchen and an amphibious vehicle. It's the one place where the building fills the frame. Streets like Zemgales iela are lined with weathered brick and Soviet-era buildings, many abandoned, so treat them as a quieter extra stop.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: For a moody warm-up, stand on Zemgales iela, 559 m from the prison with the prison to the west, and face the weathered brick and Soviet-era buildings. For the main shot, walk into the yard of Karostas cietums and face the red-brick building and the watchtower near the entrance.

selfie_spots.detail: in the prison yard, next to the old military vehicle on display

selfie_research.safety: Some of the old Tsarist-era brick buildings in Karosta are boarded up or look unsafe to enter, so don't go inside them for a quick look.
selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole prison in frame, so ask_someone_spot is null. The only selfie spot is a courtyard photo opportunity from a user-compiled listing; no page confirms the prison building is in the background there, so treat it as doubtful. The Oskars Kalpaka swing bridge (Oskara Kalpaka tilts) is a named place near the prison, but no page says the prison is visible from it. Nothing I found states selfie stick or tripod rules. The Airial page says photography is generally allowed in public areas but staff should be asked about restrictions; that is a general photo rule, not a selfie-stick or tripod rule, so I left it out of rules. The 'Karosta Forts' photo spot on Locationscout is a different site. The prison's address is Invalīdu iela 4, Liepāja, and the coordinates you gave were not checked against any page.

card.hook: Picture a gold-domed cathedral plonked in the middle of plain grey Soviet flats. That's Karosta, and the clash is the whole photo.
card.stand_here: Stand in front of the main facade of Sv. Nikolaja Jūras katedrāle (the Orthodox naval cathedral), on the Studentu rotas iela 7 side. Face the building, and leave a strip of the flats in the frame.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get the whole facade with some of the flats around it. If you're close and it won't fit, drop to 0.5x. For just the domes against the sky, try 2x to 5x, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the golden domes, then drag the slider down to make the picture a bit darker, so the gold keeps its detail and the sky doesn't turn white.
card.best_time: Clear daylight shows off the gold best. Early morning or late afternoon should give softer, warmer light on the domes.
card.selfie_here: For a selfie, head to the Karosta Northern Forts, the concrete ruins by the sea. Climb up a little, use the front camera (or 0.5x if you want more in), and keep the fort structures over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: The outside of the cathedral is fine to photograph, but it's a place of worship and the inside is restricted, so check the official site if you want to go in. The Northern Forts have uneven ground and some climbing, so wear sturdy shoes.
card.challenge: Get gold and grey in one shot, with the domes shining and the plain blocks lurking behind, and don't let the cathedral lean.
card.good_to_know: Karosta was built as a naval base between 1890 and 1906 for Tsar Alexander III. Later it became a closed Soviet military town, with more than 20,000 people living here at its busiest. The Soviet forces left in 1994, and much of the area was left to decay.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in front of the main facade of Sv. Nikolaja Jūras katedrāle (the Orthodox naval cathedral), on the Studentu rotas iela 7 side. Face the building, and leave a strip of the flats in the frame.

selfie_spots.name: Karosta Northern Forts (concrete fort ruins by the sea)
selfie_spots.detail: on the concrete fort ruins along the seafront, climbing up a little for the best angle with the fort structures behind you
selfie_spots.why: Guides describe the Northern Forts as the main photo area of Karosta, with street art on the concrete and waves against the walls, and say some climbing is needed for the best shots.

selfie_spots.name: Liepāja letters on the Northern Breakwater (Ziemeļu mols, Karosta)
selfie_spots.detail: at the Liepāja letter sculpture on the Northern Breakwater, Ziemeļu mols, Karosta
selfie_spots.why: This is a named Karosta landmark where a phone selfie with the Liepāja letters as the backdrop is recommended, though Karosta itself is not the main background here.

rules.rule: Photography is generally allowed in public areas of the Karosta Prison, especially for guests or people on a tour, but you should check with staff for any specific restrictions.

selfie_research.safety: Terrain at the Northern Forts can be uneven and some climbing is needed for the best photo spots, so wear sturdy shoes.
selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a specific spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole Karosta landmark, so ask_someone_spot is null. The Northern Forts entry is based on general guide descriptions rather than a named viewpoint, and the Breakwater letters spot is a Liepāja landmark with the sea as backdrop rather than Karosta behind you. The Karosta Prison yard is said to have photo opportunities near an old military car, but no page describes it as a selfie spot, so I left it out. The selfie-stick and tripod advice I found is a recommendation for low light, not a stated rule, so I did not list it under rules. Source ages vary; some pages are several years old.

card.hook: Picture a row of plain grey apartment blocks, and then, out of nowhere, a church with golden domes. That's Karosta, and the clash is the whole reason this photo works.
card.stand_here: Walk into the grounds in front of the main facade, on the Studentu rotas iela 7 side, and step back a little from the building. Face the church so the big central dome and the four smaller ones all fit in your frame.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole cathedral in. If you're close and the domes won't fit, switch to 0.5x. Then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for a closer shot of the golden domes and the decoration.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the golden domes and slide it a touch darker so the gilding doesn't turn white against a bright sky.
card.best_time: Go around sunrise or sunset, when the low golden light flatters the outside of the building. It's a great excuse to make the golden domes extra golden.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold the phone a bit lower and further out. Turn so the cathedral sits over your shoulder, and check the domes aren't chopped off at the top before you tap.
card.rules_and_safety: This is an active place of worship and photography inside isn't allowed, so take all your pictures from outside.
card.challenge: Take one shot of the golden domes with a strip of grey apartment block at the edge of the frame, and see if you can make the contrast look deliberate.
card.good_to_know: The cathedral was built in the style of 17th-century Russian churches and finished in 1903 for the Russian navy based here. Vasily Kosyakov designed it. In Soviet times it was used as a gymnasium and a cinema, and the first service after it went back to the Orthodox Church was held in December 1991.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Walk into the grounds in front of the main facade, on the Studentu rotas iela 7 side, and step back a little from the building. Face the church so the big central dome and the four smaller ones all fit in your frame.

selfie_spots.name: Park beside the St. Nicholas Naval Cathedral (no proper name given in sources)
selfie_spots.detail: in the park next to the cathedral, on Studentu rotas iela 7 side; no exact spot inside the park is named
selfie_spots.why: The sources describe the park beside the cathedral as a pleasant green area with picturesque views, but none says where to stand for a selfie with the cathedral behind.

selfie_research.notes: Weak result: no page names a specific selfie or photographer spot, so the only selfie entry is the generic park beside the cathedral, which is not findable by its own name. Liepāja's cathedral is not the same as St. Petersburg's St. Nicholas Naval Cathedral, so the 'St. Nicholas Square' tips from the St. Petersburg airial page were excluded. Pages disagree on the street number (7 for Studentu rotas iela / Katedrāles iela, 2 for Katedrāles iela on Wikimedia Commons). Pages say photography inside the cathedral is prohibited or discouraged, which is not a selfie-stick or tripod rule, so it is not listed under rules. No page gives selfie-stick or tripod rules, and no page gives a safety point.

card.hook: Nothing about this building stands up straight, and that's the whole charm. The glass walls lean back and scoop up the sky, so no two photos look quite the same.
card.stand_here: Head for the area near Jūras iela and stand about 15 m north of the numbered pin, at the phone icon on the map. Face south and the leaning glass is right in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x so the whole cone and its tilted glass fit in one shot. Then try zoom 1x for a tighter view, and zoom 2x or more to pick out a patch of glass and its reflections.
card.make_it_pop: Tap a bright patch of glass, then slide it a little darker so the sky reflections keep their detail.
card.best_time: Go on a bright day with some cloud, when the glass shows sky and cloud patterns without harsh glare. Late afternoon is also said to give the amber glass a lovely glow, and if the building is lit after dark, switch on night mode and rest your phone against something firm.
card.selfie_here: Walk the outside walkway beside the amber glass panels (Radio iela 8) and turn so the building fills the frame behind you. One 2016 reviewer rated it, so it's worth a quick check on site. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold it a little low so the glass leans over your shoulder. The Liepāja Promenade nearby is another option, with the hall as your backdrop, and sunset is the time to try it.
card.rules_and_safety: The outside is fine to photograph from the area around it, but for events or anything inside, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take a shot at zoom 2x or more where the glass fills the whole frame, with no ground in sight, so it looks like the sky has been tipped sideways.
card.good_to_know: The Great Amber Concert Hall (Lielais Dzintars in Latvian) is Liepāja's concert hall and arts centre. The Liepāja Symphony Orchestra is based here. In March 2016 it hosted the 24th Liepaja International Stars Festival for the first time.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the area near Jūras iela and stand about 15 m north of the numbered pin, at the phone icon on the map. Face south and the leaning glass is right in front of you.

selfie_spots.why: A 2016 Tripadvisor reviewer recommends walking the outside walkway to watch the light change through the amber glass, so the building itself fills the frame behind you.

card.hook: Almost 55 metres of tower is a lot to squeeze into a phone screen, and it loves to lean if you tilt up to fit it all in. Let's keep it standing straight.
card.stand_here: Stand near Lielā iela, about 110 m south-west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face north-east. From here you can fit the whole tower in the frame with room around it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the whole church with the tower rising behind the main body. If the whole church won't fit, take a second shot at zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) of the clock and the top of the tower.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on gridlines and line the tower up with a vertical grid line so it stands straight, with a little sky above it and some ground below.
card.best_time: Pick a day when the light is falling on the front of the church. Late afternoon or early evening may suit this side best, but check how the light looks when you arrive.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone has it, and hold the phone a little low so the tower rises over your shoulder. Keep the phone upright so the tower doesn't lean.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the outside from the street. Going inside, tours and the tower may have set times or tickets, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the tower dead straight on a grid line, then zoom in for a second shot of the clock and see if you can beat your first one.
card.good_to_know: The city council decided to build this Lutheran church in 1742 for the German community, and it was consecrated on 5 December 1758. The tower was raised to almost 55 metres in 1865-1866. Inside, the 1779 organ has 131 stops and over 7000 pipes, and it was the largest mechanical organ in the world until 1968.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand near Lielā iela, about 110 m south-west of the subject, at the phone icon on the map, and face north-east. From here you can fit the whole tower in the frame with room around it.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a street, square, steps, or garden where a visitor can stand with Holy Trinity Cathedral behind them, so I have no selfie spot to report. The only vantage named is the cathedral's 55 m tower (reached via the church, around 3 EUR per Wanderlog, and reported closed on at least one visit), but that is a view from the landmark, not a spot with the cathedral in the background, so I left it out. No page names a spot for a passer-by to photograph the visitor with the whole church, so ask_someone_spot is null. No page states selfie stick or tripod rules, so rules is empty. Sources conflict on the address: Tripjive places the cathedral on Brīvības iela, while the official city site, Evendo, and Wikivoyage give Lielā iela 9. Tripadvisor reviews mention the building was under reconstruction, which may be out of date. Wanderlog and Tripadvisor both say photos are not allowed inside, but that is an interior photography rule, not a selfie stick or tripod rule, so I did not list it.

card.hook: Theatres are great subjects because they just stand there and look important. Liepāja Theatre has been doing exactly that since 1907, with a solid frontage, doorways and maybe a poster or two.
card.stand_here: Use the map to head for Liepāja Theatre (Liepājas teātris). It's about 3 minutes on foot. Take your first shot from where you are, facing the building square on, then walk closer for a second one.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to fit the whole front in. If the theatre looks small from where you stand, try 2x or more to fill the frame without moving. Use 0.5x only if you walk right up and can't fit the building in.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line up the edges of the walls with the vertical lines, and keep your phone level so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Daytime is best, when the whole front is easy to see. A bright overcast day is lovely too, because the light is even and there are no harsh shadows. If you're in town for a performance, an evening visit adds atmosphere, and night mode can help if the building is lit.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, stand with the theatre front behind you and keep your arm a bit lower and out to the side so the building peeks over your shoulder. Try 0.5x if you want more of the building in the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: You can photograph the outside from the street. If you want to see inside or catch a performance, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one straight-on shot of the whole front, then a second closer one on the entrance with any sign or poster you can spot.
card.good_to_know: Liepāja Theatre (Liepājas teātris) is the town's theatre and has been going since 1907. It's a working theatre, so it can be busier on performance evenings. That's good for atmosphere but harder for a clean view.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Use the map to head for Liepāja Theatre (Liepājas teātris). It's about 3 minutes on foot. Take your first shot from where you are, facing the building square on, then walk closer for a second one.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with Liepāja Theatre behind the photographer, or a spot for a passer-by to photograph a visitor with the whole theatre in frame, so both fields are empty rather than guessed. Pages checked: liepaja.travel city map (https://liepaja.travel/en/useful/city-map/), latvia.travel (https://www.latvia.travel/en/sight/liepaja-theatre), Tripadvisor (https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g274965-d2322333-Reviews-Liepaja_Theater-Liepaja_Kurzeme_Region.html), AB3D Architects project page (https://www.ab3d.lv/eng/projects/liepaja-theater/), and a Mapcarta entry (https://mapcarta.com/W294324174). Possible leads, not usable as answers: the liepaja.travel sightseeing page (https://liepaja.travel/en/see-do/sightseeing/) lists a 'Liepāja' letters sculpture at Jānis Čakste Square for selfies, but it is framed as a beach-letters photo, not with the theatre behind. The AB3D page places the theatre on the square by Teātra Street next to Holy Trinity Church, but does not call it a photo spot. The Holy Trinity Cathedral tower (https://liepaja.travel/en/see-and-do/holy-trinity-cathedral/) offers a city panorama, but that is a viewpoint, not a theatre view. Photo-spot sites (locationscout, photohound) did not name a theatre spot. A local search for a named photo spot on Teātra iela or Rožu laukums would be the next step.

card.hook: This slim iron tower was hit by sixteen shells in the First World War, and you can still spot the dents. Walk up and play detective.
card.stand_here: Stand on Dienvidu mols, the south pier. The lighthouse is to the south-east, about 440 m away, so face that way and keep the tower in the middle of your screen.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the tower with the harbour around it. Then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the metal sheets, and use 0.5x only if you want lots of pier and port in the shot.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the tower on one of the vertical lines, with a bit of pier or water in front. If the sky is bright and the tower looks dark, tap the tower, then slide the brightness a little darker so the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: A clear afternoon or early evening should give you the best light on the side of the tower you can see. Try to skip midday, when the sky is at its whitest.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera at 0.5x and turn so the tower stands tall behind your shoulder. Hold the phone with both hands and take a few shots in a row, because the wind won't help.
card.rules_and_safety: The pier is an open outdoor walk and can be breezy, so hold your phone with both hands. The tower itself may not be open to visitors, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Zoom in on the newer iron sheets and find the letters KOD, then get a photo of them with the tower still in view.
card.good_to_know: The tower was built in 1868 from cast iron made by melting down ship wreckage. The dents from the German light cruiser SMS Augsburg's shells can still be seen in the outer cladding. The letters KOD on some newer sheets stand for Liepāja.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Dienvidu mols, the south pier. The lighthouse is to the south-east, about 440 m away, so face that way and keep the tower in the middle of your screen.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where the Liepāja Lighthouse is behind a visitor, so I have no selfie spot or passer-by spot to report. Wanderlog (https://wanderlog.com/place/details/1214697/liep%C4%81ja-lighthouse) says the lighthouse is closed to visitors as of late 2025 and can only be viewed from the shore; it also says some travelers photographed it from a rented boat, which is not a mappable spot, so I left it out. Vytis Tours (https://vytistours.com/things-to-do-in-liepaja-latvia/) says you can climb to a viewing balcony, which conflicts with Wanderlog and Trek.zone (https://trek.zone/en/latvia/places/192556/liepaja-lighthouse), which say the interior is not generally open; I did not use it. The Northern Breakwater (https://www.latvia.travel/en/sight/northern-breakwater) is named as a sunset-watching spot, but no page puts the lighthouse in frame there. The ibiblio page (https://www.ibiblio.org/lighthouse/lvaw.htm) mentions a good view from a street, but it describes a different light on Turaidas Street, not this one. Trek.zone also flags a high crime rate in a neighbourhood about 35 minutes' walk away; that is not tied to any photo spot, so I left it out of the safety field. Suggest checking locally for a shore viewpoint before relying on this.
